faq.question: Who can enroll in the Content Creator Professional program?
faq.answer: The program is designed for aspiring content creators, social media producers, digital marketing students, graphic designers, video editing beginners, entrepreneurs, business owners, and freelance creators who want to master practical, end-to-end commercial content production.

faq.question: Is prior video editing or graphic design experience required?
faq.answer: No. The course begins with foundational principles of visual communication, composition, and storytelling. It progressively builds up to professional desktop editing in Adobe Premiere Pro and graphic design in Adobe Photoshop. Basic computer literacy and smartphone familiarity are the only prerequisites.

faq.question: Is a professional DSLR or mirrorless camera compulsory?
faq.answer: No. A modern smartphone capable of recording 1080p or 4K video is fully sufficient for all practical cinematography exercises. We teach students how to unlock manual camera controls (exposure, shutter speed, focus peaking, white balance) using mobile manual tools like Blackmagic Cam.

faq.question: Which primary desktop video editing software is taught in the course?
faq.answer: Adobe Premiere Pro is the primary desktop non-linear editor (NLE) taught in the program. Students learn media ingestion, vertical 9:16 sequence architecture, ripple/rolling edits, J/L cuts, speed ramping, Lumetri Color balancing, Essential Sound audio mixing, and automated speech-to-text captions.

faq.question: Is Adobe Photoshop taught in the course?
faq.answer: Yes. Adobe Photoshop is the primary raster graphic design and photo retouching tool taught in Module 10. Students master non-destructive layer masking, Pen Tool product cutouts, smart objects, realistic contact/cast shadows, and typography styling for social media.

faq.question: Why is Canva included alongside Adobe Photoshop?
faq.answer: Canva Pro is taught as a rapid, agile production tool for collaborative agency workflows, Brand Kit implementation, fast template customization, and team review processes. Photoshop provides pixel-level creative precision, while Canva enables high-velocity content scaling.

faq.question: Is Instagram Edits included in the curriculum?
faq.answer: Yes. Module 11 covers the Meta 'Edits' standalone application and native Instagram creator tools for on-device mobile editing, teleprompter recording, trending audio synchronization, and mobile-first exports.

faq.question: Are original footage-based videos compulsory?
faq.answer: Yes. Physical filming is a core pillar of the course. At least 5 of the 8 completed short-form videos must be primarily filmed from original physical student footage. Stock footage or pure AI video cannot replace practical production assessments.

faq.question: How many completed videos are produced in the program?
faq.answer: Students produce exactly eight distinct completed commercial short-form videos across the program: three in Month 2 (Talking-head, Product demo, Cinematic lifestyle), three in Month 3 (two high-retention edits + one hybrid AI-assisted video), and two in Month 4 (two distinct UGC-style ad variants).

faq.question: Are all eight completed videos different?
faq.answer: Yes. Each video represents a distinct commercial format, concept, and script. Different aspect-ratio exports (e.g. 4:5 or 1:1 crops of a 9:16 master) are documented as multi-format adaptations and are strictly not counted as additional videos.

faq.question: Are six static social graphics and two multi-slide carousels required?
faq.answer: Yes. Students produce six professional static social posts in Adobe Photoshop (.psd + exports) and two complete five-slide branded educational carousels in Canva/Photoshop as mandatory visual portfolio evidence.

faq.question: Is product photography included in the curriculum?
faq.answer: Yes. Module 07 is entirely dedicated to commercial tabletop product photography, macro staging, reflection management (glass, plastic, metal), lifestyle prop styling, uncompressed RAW capture, and color calibration.

faq.question: Is motion graphics covered in the course?
faq.answer: Introductory motion graphics are covered in Module 11, focusing on keyframing position and scale, animated lower thirds, callout boxes, and tracked feature highlights using Premiere Pro's Essential Graphics panel.

faq.question: Is advanced Adobe After Effects mastery included?
faq.answer: No. Advanced 3D motion design, complex visual effects (VFX), and advanced compositing in After Effects are outside the scope of this course. These advanced disciplines are covered in our specialized Video Editing & Motion Graphics program.

faq.question: What artificial intelligence tools are taught in the course?
faq.answer: Adobe Firefly is the primary commercial generative AI platform taught for image generation and Generative Fill. Students also gain supervised exposure to Runway Gen-3 / Kling for atmospheric video B-roll, ElevenLabs for ethical voice synthesis, and ChatGPT for ideation.

faq.question: Are Adobe Firefly generative credits provided?
faq.answer: Instruction includes guided demonstrations and practical lab exercises using institutional accounts. Students learn prompt efficiency and credit budgeting to maximize standard personal or educational Creative Cloud allocations.

faq.question: Are paid subscriptions to Runway, Kling, or ElevenLabs mandatory?
faq.answer: No. Paid personal subscriptions to third-party AI platforms are not required. The course provides supervised lab demonstrations and utilizes free-tier or institutional demonstration accounts for selective practical exposure.

faq.question: Are AI-generated assets commercially usable?
faq.answer: Adobe Firefly native models are trained on licensed Adobe Stock content and designed for commercial safety. However, partner foundation models integrated into Firefly and third-party tools carry differing licensing conditions and commercial risks, which are rigorously audited in Module 12.

faq.question: Are real client brands required for the projects?
faq.answer: Students may choose either an approved real brand (e.g. a local business, personal brand, or client) or develop a structured, realistic commercial brand concept. Both options follow identical commercial brief standards.

faq.question: What is a UGC-style advertisement?
faq.answer: User-Generated Content (UGC) ads are creator-led, authentic-looking video advertisements filmed vertically on smartphones that demonstrate products, solve common consumer problems, and provide genuine reviews rather than glossy corporate commercials.

faq.question: Are live paid advertising campaigns included?
faq.answer: No. Students learn the creative architecture, scripting (PAS framework), and variant production for paid ads, but the course does not require students to spend money funding live ad campaigns.

faq.question: Is paid ad account management taught in this course?
faq.answer: Technical media buying, ad budget optimization, and pixel management are covered in our Digital Marketing Professional course. This course focuses on creative production, video editing, and performance creative variants.

faq.question: Is social media publishing covered?
faq.answer: Yes. Module 14 covers scheduling workflows, caption writing, social SEO, metadata tagging, cover selection, and publishing operations using Meta Business Suite and native creator dashboards.

faq.question: Is content performance analytics covered?
faq.answer: Yes. Module 14 covers organic and commercial analytics: reach, impressions, retention curves, average viewing duration, saves, shares, and click-through rate (CTR) concepts using Instagram Professional Dashboard and YouTube Studio.

faq.question: Is a real follower or viral reach result required to pass?
faq.answer: No. Academic evaluation is based entirely on observable creative craft, technical production quality, strategic depth, and compliance. Student grades are never tied to social media algorithm views, follower counts, or viral luck.

faq.question: Does the course guarantee client projects or job placements?
faq.answer: No. Nova Skills provides practical career guidance, client pitching templates, media kit design, and portfolio development, but does not make unverified promises or false guarantees of employment, income, or clients.

faq.question: What is the final capstone project?
faq.answer: The final capstone is the Integrated Brand Content Campaign, an end-to-end commercial portfolio encompassing 15 evidence categories: strategy briefs, 30-day calendar, 5 AV scripts, 8 short-form videos, 6 static designs, 2 carousels, 6 product photos, AI logs, and client handover files.

faq.question: Are editable source files required for portfolio submissions?
faq.answer: Yes. Students must organize and submit editable Adobe Premiere Pro project files (.prproj), layered Photoshop files (.psd), and Canva shareable links to demonstrate true non-destructive technical craftsmanship.

faq.question: What certificate is awarded upon completion?
faq.answer: Students who achieve at least 70% cumulative score across the 7 assessment domains receive the official Nova Skills Professional Certificate in Content Creation & Brand Production, subject to actual institute approval.

faq.question: What is the course fee?
faq.answer: The standard institutional tuition fee is INR 24,900. Nova Skills upholds 100% transparent pricing with zero artificial countdown timers, fake discounts, or inflated reference pricing.

faq.question: Is statutory GST extra on the course fee?
faq.answer: Yes. Applicable statutory GST (18%: INR 4,482; Total: INR 29,382) is extra, as clearly stated on all institutional enrollment documents.

faq.question: Is an EMI or installment plan available?
faq.answer: Flexible installment or third-party EMI options are subject to financial partner credit approval at enrollment and are not an automatic institutional entitlement.

faq.question: How is this course different from YouTube Growth & Content Strategy Professional?
faq.answer: YouTube Growth (Course 27) specializes in long-form 16:9 video, YouTube Studio recommendation algorithms, audience retention analytics, and YouTube Partner Program (YPP) monetization. Content Creator Professional (Course 28) focuses on multi-platform short-form vertical video (Reels, Shorts), product photography, Photoshop design, and direct-response UGC ads.

faq.question: How is this course different from Generative AI Video Production?
faq.answer: Generative AI Video Production focuses on advanced AI-first filmmaking, text-to-video world building, and cinematic commercial generation. Course 28 prioritizes physical camera filming, real lighting, and authentic human presentation, deploying AI strictly as a supervised creative accelerator.

faq.question: How is this course different from Video Editing & Motion Graphics?
faq.answer: Video Editing & Motion Graphics is a dedicated post-production program focused on complex multicam editing, advanced After Effects motion design, 3D tracking, and broadcast VFX. Course 28 is an end-to-end creator program covering strategy, camera shooting, lighting, audio, design, editing, and client delivery.

faq.question: How is this course different from Digital Marketing Professional?
faq.answer: Digital Marketing Professional focuses on paid ad campaign management (Meta Ads Manager, Google Ads), media buying, conversion funnels, SEO, email automation, and analytics. Content Creator Professional focuses on the creative content assets—producing the actual videos, graphics, and copy that fuel marketing campaigns.
